name: nimbus
description: HIPAA security review of a Knack app's structure: which fields hold patient data, which pages and roles can reach them, and what to fix.

interface.longDescription:
Nimbus reviews how a Knack app is built and finds the mistakes that can expose patient data: pages without a login that show patient fields, forms anyone can use to change records, roles that can see more than they should, and platform settings to check. Each finding names the page, view or setting and what to change in the Knack Builder.

In chat you can review which fields hold patient data (PHI), record those decisions, see the findings and the access matrix by role, and re-check the app after a change.

Nimbus reads the app's structure only. It never reads, receives or returns patient records or other record data, and it never changes the Knack app.

To use it, create a Nimbus account at nimbus.avvera.ca and register your Knack app there.
defaultPrompt: Help me get started with Nimbus for Knack
Review my Knack app for HIPAA risks and show me the most serious findings.
Which user roles can see patient data in my Knack app?

positive.prompt: Which Knack apps are registered in my Nimbus account?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists one app, EMR (6ae9e2318188fcdc92b39c6e), active and verified.

positive.prompt: Give me the HIPAA assessment summary for my Knack app EMR.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports 3 critical findings (patient data accessible without login on the public "Patient Directory" page, and a form with no login that edits existing PHI records), high-priority reviews (Data Access Control set up but not enforced, every logged-in user can see patient data on "Account Settings"), and coverage warnings to check in the builder.

positive.prompt: Explain the most serious finding in my Knack app EMR and what I should change in the Knack Builder.
positive.expected_behavior: Names the critical finding "Patient data accessible without login": the public page "Patient Directory" shows Patient fields (name, email, phone, birthdate) to anyone with the URL, and says to require a login on that page or remove the view.

positive.prompt: Which tables in my Knack app EMR hold patient data, and is anything still undecided?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the PHI tables (Patient, Prescriptions, Appointments, Appointment Notes, Allergies, Vaccinations, Lab Reports, Family History, Messages), the staff tables marked not PHI, and one open question about the Accounts email field.

positive.prompt: Show which user roles in my Knack app EMR can see or change patient data.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the access matrix for the PHI fields: for each role (Any Authenticated User, Doctor, Nurse, Office Manager, Practice Owner, Front & Back Office Staff, Patient) what it can do with each field today (view, add, edit, delete), and that no intended access has been set yet.

negative.prompt: Show me the names and birthdates of the patients in my Knack app EMR.
negative.expected_behavior: Says Nimbus reads the app's structure only and never reads or returns record data, so it cannot list patients.

negative.prompt: Fix the public Patient Directory page in my Knack app EMR for me by adding a login.
negative.expected_behavior: Says Nimbus never changes a Knack app; explains the change to make in the Knack Builder (require a login on the page or remove the view) for the user to do.

negative.prompt: Subscribe me to the annual plan and add a third app to my Nimbus account.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not take payment or start a subscription in chat; says plans and extra apps are described on the Nimbus website. No price and no checkout link in the answer.

publication.release_notes: First public release: HIPAA structure review of Knack apps: PHI inventory, findings, access matrix.
